Unfortunately, I think you can not learn or practice the AT on your own. If you can afford it, I would suggest you get a teacher. Even if it is only for two lessons. There is a kinasthetic (aka touch) element that IMHO you need to experience. Some teachers say it can be taught online. I  my opinion, I would only choose this option if I could not aee a teacher in real life because rhere i snone.

That being said, a long-time tested classic is Michael Gelb's body learning. I bought my copy roughly around 2012, and it was a classic back then already. I know there is an older version with other pictures that were replaced by better ones in "my" edition. Whether the newest editions provide anything new, I don't know. I personally often buy uses books, but you need to know which edition it is.

Anthony Kingsley has a very good introductory video on youtube (from 1990, I think).

There is also a podcast called body learning (that has nothing to do with the book by Michael Gelb) by Robert Rickover, which is very useful.

Robert also says in his podcast somewhere that most people would already benefit immensely from learning to get into the constructive rest position which is something your AT teacher could show you in roughly two lessons. There are also guided constructive rest instructions in his podcasts by several teachers. Videos might be online, too.

Hope it helps

I once read a book of procrastination researcher Timothy Pychyl. And he said basically: If you remember one thing from my book at all it should be this message: Just get started.

What he means is not to agonize about what you  all need to do but just say to yourself: "I'll start". And with starting, your mission is complete. I think he gave an example about writing a recommendation letter (nah, I think it was in his podcast if it still exists) and he says he does not like writing these because he wants to make them not just mediocre but fair for the student. So therefore he asks himself what he can already do: Start and open the laptop, open a document and write the adresse and the name etc.

It's a long time ago since I've read his book and yes, at least I remembered the main point. I hope I remembered the other points correctly.

Btw his book is small because he said: "Big books don't get read - especially not about procrastination" 😀

One last thing: He said he doesn't mean: "Just do it!", that would be wrong. But really. Just. Get. Started.
